sub_answers.sub_question: What injuries or durability concerns affected Randy Johnson and how did they limit his availability or effectiveness?
sub_answers.text: Johnson was sidelined much of the 1996 season with a back injury that limited his availability that year [d386384s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What criticisms did contemporaries or commentators raise about Johnson's control, temperament, or interactions with hitters?
sub_answers.text: Opponents and observers described Johnson as intimidating, with Larry Walker saying Johnson 'almost killed me' after facing him in spring training and reacting theatrically when Johnson threw over his head in the All-Star Game [d386384s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: Were there notable on-field incidents, ejections, or controversies involving Randy Johnson documented in his career?
sub_answers.text: In the 1997 All-Star Game Johnson theatrically threw over Larry Walker's head, an on-field incident that drew widespread reaction and laughter from players and fans [d386384s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How did any statistical limitations—such as walk rates, ERA fluctuations, or platoon splits—temper assessments of Johnson's dominance?
sub_answers.text: Johnson showed clear platoon variation with Larry Walker batting .393 in 28 career at-bats against him compared with left-handed hitters overall batting .199 against Johnson [d386384s7p0]. The velocity of his fastball and slider declined in later years from as high as 102 mph to around 96 mph for the fastball and about 87 mph for the slider, reflecting a decrease in his raw stuff over time [d386384s16p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: In what ways did Randy Johnson contribute to team win totals, division titles, or postseason appearances during his tenure?
sub_answers.text: Johnson led the Arizona Diamondbacks to the playoffs in 1999 while posting a 17–9 record, a 2.48 ERA and 364 strikeouts that season [d386384s9p0]. Johnson produced high-win seasons that directly increased team win totals, including 19 wins in 2000 and a 24–5 season in 2002 [d386384s9p0][d386384s11p0]. Johnson and Curt Schilling together anchored the Diamondbacks rotation, providing a two-ace core that supported postseason contention [d386384s9p0]. Johnson’s dominant stretches with the Mariners (for example a 20–4 1997 season and a 53–9 run between 1994–1997) also contributed substantially to team success during those years [d386384s7p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What team pitching records or franchise milestones were set or approached while Randy Johnson was on those rosters?
sub_answers.text: Johnson extended and set MLB pitching milestones by recording multiple consecutive 300-strikeout seasons, establishing a record for the most consecutive 300+ strikeout seasons [d386384s11p0]. Johnson won multiple Cy Young Awards in both leagues and led the majors in innings, complete games and strikeouts in 1999, marking franchise-leading pitching performances [d386384s9p0]. In 2002 Johnson won the pitching Triple Crown (leading the NL in wins, ERA and strikeouts) and became the first pitcher in baseball history to post a 24–5 record [d386384s11p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: How did managers and pitching staffs utilize Johnson in rotations and postseason series to maximize team outcomes?
What observable effects did Johnson's strikeout ability have on opposing lineups and game strategies?
sub_answers.text: Opposing players sometimes avoided facing Johnson altogether, as exemplified by Larry Walker choosing not to play when scheduled to face him and expressing real concern about facing Johnson’s velocity [d386384s7p0]. Johnson’s exceptional strikeout totals (including seasons of 347, 364 and multiple 300-strikeout campaigns) produced outs via strikeouts at rates that removed balls in play and altered opposing lineup outcomes [d386384s9p0][d386384s11p0]. Teammates and catchers credited Johnson’s intensity and ‘stuff’ with elevating catcher performance and game preparation, implying his strikeout ability changed in-game dynamics for both teams [d28263789s3p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What major pitching records and milestones did Randy Johnson achieve during his career?
sub_answers.text: Johnson was 6 feet 10 inches tall, making him the tallest player in MLB history when he entered the league [d386384s0p0]. He led his league in strikeouts nine times and set the record for most consecutive seasons with 300 or more strikeouts, including six 300-strikeout seasons (tied with Nolan Ryan) [d386384s0p0][d386384s11p0]. He threw a perfect game at age 40 and is one of five pitchers to have no-hitters in both leagues [d386384s12p0][d386384s0p0]. He won the pitching Triple Crown in 2002 and won four consecutive Cy Young Awards from 1999–2002 (five Cy Youngs total) [d386384s11p0][d386384s0p0].

sub_answers.sub_question: What pitches composed Randy Johnson's repertoire and which was considered his most effective strikeout pitch?
sub_answers.text: Johnson's repertoire included a high-velocity fastball, a signature slider, a split-finger fastball (changeup-like), and a sinker.[d386384s16p0]  His most effective strikeout pitch was his slider, which had tight late break and was thrown in the low 90s, causing hitters to swing through or miss as it broke just before the plate.[d386384s16p0]

How did Johnson adapt his mechanics or pitch selection over his career in response to aging or injury?
sub_answers.text: Later in his career Johnson's fastball velocity declined from as high as 102 mph to the mid-90s and his slider velocity fell to around 87 mph, reflecting a loss of pure fastball heat with age.[d386384s16p0]  He continued to employ offspeed offerings such as a split-finger fastball and a sinker to induce ground balls as his primary pitches slowed.[d386384s16p0]  Johnson also underwent back surgery (removal of a disc) and returned to pitch after rehabilitation, including mixing in unorthodox or situational pitches (an eephus was thrown in one game) during later appearances.[d386384s14p0][d386384s14p0]
